residual_risks: updateAddrs with an empty address list (clientconn.go:990-996): the spawned resetTransportAndUnlock sets Connecting, tryAllAddrs over zero addrs returns a nil error (firstConnErr never set), and the code takes the 'Success' path, leaving the addrConn in Connecting with no transport. Behavior is unchanged by this diff (pre-existing); the new lock hand-off does not make it worse.

The mutex now crosses goroutines in updateAddrs (locked in caller, unlocked in the spawned goroutine). This was checked and is safe: acbw.updateState uses serializer.Schedule (non-blocking), the deferred transport.GracefulClose -> onClose only waits briefly for the lock and returns early because its ctx is the old, cancelled ac.ctx, and every return path in resetTransportAndUnlock unlocks exactly once. A future edit adding a blocking call between the entry and the ac.mu.Unlock() at line 1262 (e.g. via the user-supplied minConnectTimeout callback at ~1245) would run under ac.mu and would also stall the deferred GracefulClose in updateAddrs.
testing_gaps: No regression test accompanies the fix: nothing deterministically exercises two concurrent addrConn.connect() calls on an Idle addrConn (or connect racing updateAddrs) and asserts only one connection attempt/transport results. The fix relies on the flaky Test/AuthorityRevive to catch regressions.
